chunks: Ilal al-Shara'i: My father, from Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their backs, their descendants and made them bear witness against their own selves - am I not your Lord? They said: Indeed."
He said: The recognition was confirmed but they forgot the time and they will remember it one day. If it were not for that, no one would know who his Creator is nor who his Sustainer is.

key_terms.أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ: "Am I not your Lord?" (The divine question in the covenant)
key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَة: Recognition or innate knowledge of God

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the verse 'Alastu bi Rabbikum' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kulayni’s *Alal al-Shara'i* elucidates the verse of Alast by affirming that the innate recognition (Ma'rifa) of God was established in the souls of Adam's descendants, though the specific temporal context of this event was forgotten. This primordial testimony ensures that every human being inherently knows their Creator and Sustainer, serving as the foundational basis for accountability in Shia theology. The hadith highlights that without this pre-eternal covenant, no one would truly know their Maker or Provider.

en.ammaar-muslim: 9. [9/-] Ilal al-Sharai: My father from Sa’d from Muhammad b. Isa from al-Hasan b. Fadhal from Ibn Bukayr from Zurara who said:

I asked Aba Ja’far عليه السلام about the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: “When your Lord took from the Children of Adam from their backs their descendants and made them bear witness against their own selves - am I not your Lord? They said: Indeed” [7:172].

He said: The Ma’rifa (Recognition) was confirmed but they forgot the time (when this episode occurred) and they will come to remember it one day. If it were not for that no one would know who his Creator is nor who his Sustainer is.
